title: The gates did not change Allah's decree, but eased a father's heart.
subtitle: What a precaution really does

row.title: precaution controls fate
sub: if I do this, all is safe

then: The sons entered Egypt by different gates as their father said. Allah says it {trap}did not help them at all against His will{/trap}. It was {reward}a need in Ya'qub's heart{/reward} that he fulfilled. Qatadah said he had knowledge and acted on it, but most people do not know.
now: You pack the first-aid kit, read the reviews, text when you arrive. Some of it is really for your own peace of mind. {idea}That is fine. Just do not mistake it for control.{/idea}
old: If something bad happens, my precautions failed.
new: Precautions settle my heart and do my part, the outcome was always Allah's.
try: Notice one worry-habit today and say: I have done my part, the rest is with Allah.

title: I am your brother, do not grieve over what they did.
subtitle: Yusuf reveals himself to Binyamin in private
then: Yusuf honored all the brothers as guests, then {idea}met Binyamin alone{/idea} and told him his story. Ibn Kathir says he told him: {reward}grieve not for what they did to me.{/reward} He asked Binyamin to keep it secret, and planned to keep him in Egypt with honor.
now: Your younger sibling is going through what you went through with the family years ago. You could tell them every bitter detail. {idea}Or you could sit them down and say: I am here, do not be sad.{/idea}
old: When I finally speak, I will tell them how badly I was treated.
new: My first words to someone hurting can be comfort, not my old grievance.
try: Message a sibling or close friend today just to say: I am here for you.

title: The king's bowl hidden in Binyamin's bag.
subtitle: A plan to keep his brother with him
then: After supplying them, Yusuf had {idea}the king's bowl placed in Binyamin's bag{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes it was used for drinking and, in the drought, for measuring grain. Then a crier called out: {trap}O caravan, you are thieves!{/trap}
now: Sometimes a scene looks like a disaster from where you stand: a sudden transfer at work, a delayed flight, an awkward misunderstanding. {idea}You do not see the plan behind it.{/idea} It may be bringing someone together.
old: If it looks like a disaster, it must be one.
new: What looks like trouble from outside can be part of a plan for good.
try: Think of one recent setback and ask: what good might be hidden inside this?

title: What have you lost? they asked, turning back.
subtitle: The brothers face the accusation
then: Hearing the cry, the brothers turned toward the men. Ibn Kathir says they looked at the one calling out and simply asked: {idea}what is it that you have lost?{/idea} {trap}The men who once lied about Yusuf were now the ones accused.{/trap}
now: Security stops you at the shop exit. A colleague says something has gone missing from the office. Your heart races. {idea}Asking a calm question first often helps more than defending yourself loudly.{/idea}
old: When accused, I need to fight back immediately.
new: A calm question can be the strongest first answer to an accusation.
try: The next time someone challenges you, ask one calm question before you defend yourself.

title: The king's measure is missing, and a reward is offered.
subtitle: A camel-load for whoever brings it
then: The men said: {trap}we are missing the king's measuring bowl.{/trap} Whoever brings it gets {reward}a camel-load{/reward} as reward, and the herald added: I guarantee it. Ibn Kathir says this was an assurance that the reward would be delivered.
now: You lose your wallet and offer a reward online. A boss loses a file and offers credit to whoever finds it. {idea}Clear terms and a promise you will honor make people trust you.{/idea}
old: When something is lost, suspicion is the fastest route.
new: A clear offer, backed by a real guarantee, brings things to light more fairly.
try: If you promise someone something today, state it clearly and then keep it.

title: By Allah, you know we are not thieves.
subtitle: The brothers point to their own conduct
then: Accused, the brothers swore: {idea}by Allah, you know we did not come to cause corruption, and we are not thieves.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they meant: since you met us, our good conduct has shown that {reward}theft is not in our character.{/reward}
now: Your manager questions your expenses. You do not need to shout. You can say: you have seen how I work for three years. {idea}A good record speaks before you do.{/idea} So build it on the ordinary days.
old: When accused, only my words can defend me.
new: The way I behave every day becomes my defense on the hard day.
try: Do one ordinary task today so honestly that it would stand up if anyone checked.

title: And if you are lying, what is the penalty?
subtitle: The brothers are asked to set their own terms
then: Yusuf's men did not impose a punishment. They asked the brothers: {idea}what should the thief's penalty be, if you turn out to be liars?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says they asked what the punishment would be if the thief was {trap}one of them{/trap}.
now: Your child broke the rule. You ask: what do you think is fair? You are surprised how strict they are with themselves. {idea}The rules we name for others are the rules we will be held to.{/idea}
old: The penalty is for other people, so I can make it harsh.
new: The standard I set for others may be the one I am judged by.
try: Before you judge someone today, ask if you would accept the same verdict yourself.

title: Whoever has it in his bag, he himself is the price.
subtitle: The brothers pronounce their own law
then: The brothers said: {trap}he in whose bag it is found will himself be the penalty.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says this was {idea}the law of Ibrahim{/idea}, that the thief is given to the one he stole from. This is exactly what Yusuf wanted.
now: You confidently say: anyone who misses the deadline loses the bonus. Then your own task is the one that is late. {idea}Speak your rules carefully. They have a way of coming back.{/idea}
old: My strict rules are only for people who break them.
new: The law I announce with confidence can be the one that finds me.
try: Rephrase one strict rule you hold for others so you would be fine living by it too.

title: Above every knower is One who knows more.
subtitle: Allah's plan for Yusuf, and the limit of all knowledge
then: Yusuf searched their bags {idea}before his brother's{/idea} to complete the plan. Allah says: thus did We plan for Yusuf. By the king's law he could not take his brother, but {reward}by their own law he could.{/reward} Qatadah said: over every person of knowledge is someone more knowing, until all knowledge ends with Allah.
now: You are the expert in the room, the one everyone asks. Then a new hire explains something you never understood. {idea}There is always someone who knows more, and above everyone, Allah.{/idea}
old: I am the one in this room who knows best.
new: Every bit of knowledge I have sits under someone else's, and all of it under Allah's.
try: Ask someone today to teach you one thing you do not know.

title: He heard the old lie about him and kept silent.
subtitle: Yusuf holds back his reply
then: When the bowl was found, the brothers said: {trap}if he stole, a brother of his stole before{/trap}, meaning Yusuf, to distance themselves. Ibn Kathir says Yusuf {idea}kept his reply to himself{/idea} and did not say it aloud: you are in a worse position, and Allah knows best what you describe.
now: In the family group, someone brings up an old, false story about you. You know the truth. You could send the long, angry reply. {idea}Sometimes the strongest answer is the one you keep inside and leave with Allah.{/idea}
old: If someone lies about me, I must correct it immediately.
new: Not every unfair remark needs my answer; Allah knows the truth of it.
try: Next time someone says something unfair, wait before replying, and say inside: Allah knows best.

title: His father is old, take one of us instead.
subtitle: The brothers now plead for their father's heart

row.title: years ago
sub: got rid of the favored son

then: Once Binyamin was to be held, the brothers begged for mercy. Ibn Kathir says they told the 'Aziz: {idea}he has an old father who loves him{/idea}, comforted by him for the son he lost. {reward}Take one of us in his place.{/reward} We see you are a doer of good.
now: The sibling who used to be jealous of you is now the one at the hospital bed, covering your shifts. {idea}People can change.{/idea} The ones who once hurt someone can grow into the ones who protect.
old: People who did wrong once will always be like that.
new: The same people who once caused harm can grow into protectors.
try: Notice one way someone who hurt you in the past has grown, and tell them.

title: Taking the innocent for the guilty would be injustice.
subtitle: Yusuf refuses a swap
then: Yusuf answered: {idea}Allah forbid that we take anyone except the one with whom we found our property.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains, according to the judgement they gave, {trap}taking an innocent man instead would be wrongdoing.{/trap}
now: The whole class gets detention for one pupil. The team loses its bonus for one person's mistake. Someone has to pay, so anyone will do. {idea}Justice cares who.{/idea}
old: As long as someone takes the blame, the matter is settled.
new: Blaming the wrong person is its own injustice, even when it is convenient.
try: If you are tempted to punish a group for one person's fault, address only that person.

title: I will not leave until my father permits me.
subtitle: The eldest brother remembers two broken promises
then: In despair, the brothers {idea}consulted in private{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says the eldest, the one who had suggested the well over killing Yusuf, reminded them of {trap}their oath to their father{/trap} and their earlier failure with Yusuf. He said: I will not leave Egypt until my father permits me or Allah decides for me.
now: You promised your parents to look after your younger brother at university, and he has dropped out. You could just go home and shrug. {idea}Or you stay with the problem and take responsibility.{/idea}
old: If it went wrong, I can explain it away and move on.
new: A broken promise calls for owning it, not leaving it behind.
try: Think of one promise you let slip. Take one step this week to make it right.

title: We testify only to what we know.
subtitle: The honest report to their father
then: The eldest told the others to go back and say: {trap}your son has stolen{/trap}, and we testify only to what we know. Qatadah and 'Ikrimah said they meant: {idea}we did not know he would steal{/idea}. We only stated the thief's punishment.
now: Your friend asks what happened between two people at work. You saw part of it. {idea}It is tempting to fill the gaps.{/idea} Saying this is what I saw, and I do not know the rest, is a kind of honesty.
old: When I tell a story, I should give the full picture.
new: I only speak to what I know, and I admit what I cannot see.
try: When you pass on news today, add: this is only what I saw.
